steps.title: TOWARDS COMPREHENSIVE AND EFFICIENT POST SAFETY ALIGNMENT OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS VIA SAFETY PATCHING

core_judgments: The approach is positioned as a novel solution to the limitations of existing PSA methods, its novelty appears limited, as the core methodology relies on the SNIP score proposed by Lee et al. and model merging techniques previously introduced by Yu et al. and Hui et al.
The paper does not provide a thorough explanation of the unique contributions or advancements that distinguish SAFEPATCHING from these established methods.
The specific innovations and the rigor of the proposed tool remain unclear.

conclusion: The paper’s central contribution is the SAFEPATCHING framework: deriving a parameter-space “safety patch” and integrating it into an already fine-tuned backbone to improve safety while preserving utility. Bhardwaj et al. (2024) already present a very similar core idea in RESTA: they compute a safety-direction delta in parameter space and add it to a fine-tuned model to restore or improve safety, and they further manipulate this delta (e.g., rescaling/dropping components) while tracking safety–utility trade-offs. This substantially overlaps with the claimed efficient, flexible post-hoc integration of safety patches into LLM backbones. The submission adds, beyond RESTA, a more elaborate two-stage pipeline with two complementary patches derived via opposite gradient directions (one for safety enhancement, one for over-safety mitigation), plus a controllable integration mechanism; it also introduces a continual PSA evaluation protocol and explicitly targets three objectives (safety enhancement, over-safety mitigation, utility preservation) in one framework. However, these additions, while interesting, are secondary refinements around a parameter-delta safety patching paradigm that is already established by Bhardwaj et al. (2024). Given that the core mechanism is substantially prefigured, the overall novelty is not strong enough for a top-tier venue.
